25.0.0.en: Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.

25.0.1.en: 1- Lifting up the soul means drawing near to God, who is exalted above all creatures, and this is done by lifting up the mind and the heart through thinking about lofty things, that is, heavenly things and every spiritual matter, so that the mind and the heart are occupied with the knowledge of God and the spiritual virtues. The body can also be lifted up, as in the lifting up of the hands; that is, the soul is lifted up by prayer and contemplation. Therefore the priest says in the Divine Liturgy, calling to the people, "Lift up your hearts."

25.0.2.en: 2- Lifting up the soul is rising above earthly things and being occupied with them, so that a person is content with using material things in the measure of the necessary needs.

25.0.3.en: 3- Lifting up the soul is by rising above the sins that humble man and put him in a place of lowliness, and not only rising above sins but above their causes, that is, keeping away from the sinners who make the soul stumble and from evil gatherings.

25.0.4.en: 4- If a person humbles himself before God, He lifts him up, because He exalts the humble (Lk 1:52); so whoever strives for humility lifts up his soul.

25.1.0.en: 2- O my God, I trust in thee: let me not be ashamed, let not mine enemies triumph over me.

25.1.1.en: 3- Yea, let none that wait on thee be ashamed: let them be ashamed which transgress without cause.

25.1.2.en: 1- David's enemies, such as Saul and Absalom, tried to attack him and kill him without cause. But in faith he lifted up his soul to God in prayer and trusted in Him, and his heart was assured that God would keep him.

25.1.3.en: 2- The enemies of David, and the enemies of all believers, are the demons, and the sins into which they try to make people fall. So David, as a believer trusting in God, asks that He deliver him from them, so that they do not triumph but, on the contrary, are put to shame.

25.1.4.en: 3- David does not mean by the shame of the treacherous revenge on them, but he means the manifestation of divine truth and justice, so that those who believe in God and all who pray to Him and wait for His deliverance are assured. And on the contrary, the wicked take notice and return to God by repentance.

25.2.0.en: 4- Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths.

25.2.1.en: 5- Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.

25.2.2.en: 1- The ways and paths are God's commandments, the Holy Bible, the life of Christ on earth, and the lives of the prophets, the Apostles, the martyrs and the saints, which we ought to imitate.

25.2.3.en: 2- Being shown and taught the ways and paths of God requires the spirit of spiritual discipleship at the hands of the father of confession, the Fathers, and spiritual brethren. And by persevering in discipleship a person finally acquires the learning of the spiritual ways.

25.2.4.en: 3- The truth is God, and training in it is spiritual striving and all the spiritual exercises in which we must persevere, so that our knowledge of the ways of God is not theoretical knowledge but we live it practically.

25.2.5.en: 4- We have no savior in all our tribulations and needs except God, so we do not trust in anyone else, even if we have all human means. And we continue to pray and seek God throughout our lives, because "the day" means the whole lifetime. We wait for God all the day and every day. And we wait for Him by persevering in prayer, reading and every spiritual striving, confident that He is able to rescue us from our tribulation and guide us to His Kingdom.

25.3.0.en: 6- Remember, O LORD, thy tender mercies and thy lovingkindnesses; for they have been ever of old.

25.3.1.en: 7- Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions: according to thy mercy remember thou me for thy goodness' sake, O LORD.

25.3.2.en: 1- David reminds God of His readiness to have mercy on His sinful, weak children; that is, he entreats Him to pour out His mercies upon him. And this humility brings an overflow of God's mercy.

25.3.3.en: 2- David also reminds God of His promises to redeem humanity, the promises that He declared in Paradise to Eve, that her seed would bruise the serpent's head (Gen 3:15). And these promises show the divine love that has been toward man from eternity, before God created him, and then was manifested in his redemption.

25.3.4.en: 3- David asks God to forget the sins of his youth, that is, those he committed when he was a beginner in his life with God, with his knowledge of sin limited, so that He finds an excuse for him and forgives him these sins.

25.3.5.en: 4- Likewise he begs God not to remember his transgressions, which are his sins when he was grown and knew that his sin was disobedience to God, and he asks God to forgive him them by His mercy. And David's remembering of God's mercies encourages him to confess his sin, because before God's judgment every person fears and trembles and cannot speak.

25.3.6.en: 5- David reminds God of His richness in love and His generosity, that is, His goodness, that He may pour out upon him not only forgiveness but also kindness and blessings, that God may support him in the pure life with Him; for he says to Him "remember me", that is, look at my sonship and that I am a man created by Your hands and in need of You, and have compassion on me and do not look at my sins.

25.3.7.en: How beautiful it is for a person to humble himself before God and ask for His mercies, for God is very tender toward all the weak and the poor who ask Him, and pours out upon them love with a fatherhood that surpasses the mind.

25.4.0.en: 8- Good and upright is the LORD: therefore will he teach sinners in the way.

25.4.1.en: 1- God is good, indeed wholly good, and He is upright, with no sin or deviation in Him, and He wants all His children to become good. And He does not desire the death of the sinner; therefore He teaches His children goodness and uprightness.

25.4.2.en: 2- He calls four classes of His children and guides them, and the first of these classes is sinners, so He guides them to the straight way so that they leave their sins and return to the way of God. And this is by His commandments and teachings, or by removing sin from them, or by showing its hideousness so that they reject it.

25.4.3.en: 3- The word "teach" here in the Hebrew original means teaching the commandments, and what is meant is that He teaches sinners His commandments, explains them to them, and convinces them of them, so that they reject their evil thoughts, which led them to sin.

25.4.4.en: 4- The Lord is tender; so in spite of His knowledge of the sins of His children, He gives them a chance to repent, as He did with the woman caught in adultery: He did not condemn her or stone her, but after forgiving her He guided her not to return to sin.

25.5.0.en: 9- The meek will he guide in the truth: and the meek will he teach his ways.

25.5.1.en: 1- He makes the meek know the truth, that is, He makes them know Himself; for the meek are those who enjoy inner calm, and therefore they have a greater readiness than others to know God and to understand His purposes, because they are quiet like God, not attached to the world, and are not troubled by any gain or loss.

25.5.2.en: 2- The meek are humble, because meekness and humility are two virtues connected together; therefore the meek, by his humility, is ready to learn faster than others, and God pours out His knowledge upon him.

25.5.3.en: 3- In His guidance of this second class, the meek, God is not content only to guide them, but also trains them practically in walking in the truth, so that they live the commandment practically in their lives.

25.5.4.en: 4- God teaches the meek His ways, and His ways are the virtues, so He teaches them how to acquire every virtue and makes them grow in it.

25.6.0.en: 10- All the paths of the LORD are mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.

25.6.1.en: 1- God's way of dealing with His children is mercy toward all the repentant, and at the same time it is truth and justice toward all the stubborn and careless.

25.6.2.en: 2- God's mercy appears first in His coming, when He offered His salvation on the Cross, and we enjoy this mercy in our present life. But truth and justice appear in the Second Coming of Christ, that is, the Day of Judgment, on everyone who did not make use of the period of life for repentance.

25.6.3.en: 3- The third class that God teaches is those who keep His covenant and His testimonies; everyone who cares about and keeps and holds fast to God's covenants and promises and believes in them enjoys mercy, and these are what God repeated in the Holy Bible, and he demands them from Him in prayer with persistence, so he receives them and rejoices in them.

25.6.4.en: 4- God's testimonies are His commandments, and they are also the lives of the fathers in the Holy Bible, and the lives of the prophets and Apostles, and they are also the prophecies of the prophets and the teachings of the Apostles in the New Testament. And everyone who keeps them and holds fast to them, God's mercies are poured out upon him.

25.6.5.en: 5- God's mercy also includes His kindnesses, as in the Septuagint translation, that is, His gifts, His support of His children, and His various blessings that He grants to His children so that they remain holding fast to His commandments. And they are, even more, His spiritual gifts, that is, His revealing of Himself to those who keep His covenant and His testimonies, because experiencing God and feeling Him in this present life is the greatest encouragement to bear the pains of spiritual striving.

25.7.0.en: 11- For thy name's sake, O LORD, pardon mine iniquity; for it is great.

25.7.1.en: 1- God's name means His mercy, His goodness and His fatherhood, to which He referred in the preceding verse. And because of David's faith in the name of the merciful God he dared to confess his sins and ask for forgiveness.

25.7.2.en: 2- When David kept God's covenants and testimonies his mind was enlightened and he felt the greatness of his sin, so he asked for repentance and the forgiveness of his sins.

25.7.3.en: 3- David the prophet feels the greatness of his sin and that he does not deserve forgiveness, and all his good works do not give him a sufficient excuse. But his hope is only in the name of God, so his reliance is on God's grace. And this shows the extent of David's humility, and therefore God pours out upon him forgiveness and many mercies.

25.8.0.en: 12- What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose.

25.8.1.en: 1- The fourth class that God teaches is those who fear Him. When David says "What man is he that feareth the LORD?", he shows that those who fear the Lord are very few, but they exist, and they alone are saved; because the fear of God makes them keep away from sin, and know God, and enjoy His love and the sense of Him.

25.8.2.en: 2- If God finds a person who fears Him He hastens to him and teaches him the right way that He chooses for him, which is the way of life, the way of the Kingdom; that is, He guides him to keep His commandments and live with Him.

25.8.3.en: 3- If a person fears God but has strayed from the right knowledge because of any strange teachings, yet is sincere in the fear of God, God will not leave him, as He appeared to Saul of Tarsus and guided him to the faith (Acts 9:1-19); and if he is far from the knowledge of the truth, He sends someone to guide him, as He did with Cornelius the Gentile, and sent to him the Apostle Peter, who taught him and those with him, and they believed and were baptized (Acts 10:19-33).

25.9.0.en: 13- His soul shall abide in goodness; and his seed shall inherit the earth.

25.9.1.en: 1- Whoever fears God, God pours out upon him material blessings and many good things in the world, so that he lacks nothing; he lives his day, and sleeps with good things abundant around him, as He did with Abraham, who believed in God and feared Him and left the world for His sake, so He blessed him in the wilderness and gave him material goods sufficient for all his life.

25.9.2.en: 2- Among the most important of God's blessings to those who fear Him is that He blesses their seed, so that they inherit the earth; that is, God's blessings extend to the seed of those who fear Him, because the seed learned the fear of God from the fathers, so they receive a blessing and many good things also, as happened with Isaac and Jacob and the people of Israel, who inherited the land of Canaan as a free gift from God.

25.9.3.en: 3- The person who believes in God and fears Him not only abides in material good things but, rather, in spiritual good things, that is, he settles in the bosom of God, and feels His presence, and enjoys fellowship with Him and all the virtues.

25.9.4.en: 4- Spiritually also, the seed of those who fear God inherit the earth, since by their fragrant conduct they draw others to life with God, so they inherit many souls for God. This is what happened with God's people anciently, when some of the Gentiles believed and joined it, and it appeared clearly in the New Testament, when many from the various countries of the world believed in Christ at the hands of the Apostles and the believers.

25.10.0.en: 14- The secret of the LORD is for those who fear him, and his covenant is to teach them.

25.10.1.en: 1- After explaining two gifts that God gives to those who fear Him, namely that he abides in good and that his seed inherits the earth, he declares here a third gift, which is that He grants them His secret. By His secret is meant many blessings that they do not expect, so He solves their problems in a way that surpasses the mind, and gives them spiritual and material blessings, and grants them His peace in their hearts, so they are distinguished from all people by this inner peace.

25.10.2.en: 2- The secret of the Lord is the knowledge of Him, for there is nothing greater than knowing God and enjoying being with Him closely. And in the New Testament He revealed wonderful secrets about Himself when He made clear His Holy Trinity. And in every generation He makes those who fear Him know Himself, as He appeared to Moses in the bush and spoke with him throughout his life, and as He spoke to David and Solomon, and then His work grew greater in His Incarnation, and the declaring of His secrets to His disciples and all who believe in Him in the Holy Bible.

25.10.3.en: 3- The fourth gift that God gives to those who fear Him is that He declares His covenant to them, and the declaring of His covenant means the fulfillment of His promises; for all His covenants are enjoyed only by those who fear Him, whether they are material or spiritual promises, as He declared that through Moses at Mount Gerizim (Deut 11:29), and declared it again through Solomon at the dedication of the Temple (1 Kgs 8:22-53). And He declared it in the New Testament in His Sermon on the Mount (Mt 5-7) and His talks with His disciples and His intercessory prayer (Jn 14-17).

25.10.4.en: 4- Those who fear God are His close children, indeed His friends, so He rejoices to share with them as friends, as He did with Abraham and shared with him in the decision to burn Sodom and Gomorrah (Gen 18:17).

25.10.5.en: 5- God's covenant to teach those who fear Him is His teaching them the way of the Kingdom, that is, He teaches them His commandments, and how to walk uprightly, keep away from sin and hold fast to their faith, so that they receive the eternal inheritance.

25.11.0.en: 15- Mine eyes are ever toward the LORD; for he shall pluck my feet out of the net.

25.11.1.en: 1- The fifth gift that God gives to those who fear Him is that He delivers them from the snares of the devil, that is, his net. Though the devil is deceitful and strong, God is stronger than he and able to rescue those who fear Him, so they do not fear the wars of the devil, and live always at ease.

25.11.2.en: 2- In order for a person to enjoy this gift he must always lift up his eyes toward God, and this is by prayer, so that he lives in what is called constant prayer, that is, he seeks God throughout the day. It does not mean that he does no work, but that he accustoms himself to lift up his heart as much as he can to God in prayer, so he lives at ease, in addition to his enjoyment of seeing God and fellowship with Him, so he lives the Kingdom while on earth.

25.11.3.en: 3- God in His fatherhood takes care of those who fear Him, so He rescues their feet from the devil's nets, even if they do not ask Him, because they sometimes do not understand and do not know the devil's tricks, but God knows and rescues them, and keeps the nets away from them; and even if they fall as a result of negligence, God in His tenderness visits them for the salvation of their souls.

25.11.4.en: God guarantees you a life of ease, indeed full of joy, if you live in His fear. For the fear of God is a fortress that protects you from every evil and gives you happiness. Remember God at all times by prayer, and you will live in His fear.

25.12.0.en: 16- Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am alone and poor.

25.12.2.en: 1- Before the multitude of the devil's wars David feels that he needs the five preceding gifts of God, and asks Him to have mercy on him and rescue him from these wars, and to save him if he falls.

25.12.3.en: 2- David feels that his only hope is in God's looking upon him and His care for him, so he says to Him, "Turn thee unto me." And as long as God is looking at him, he is at ease, however much evil surrounds him.

25.12.4.en: 3- David declares that he is alone and poor and in need of God's mercy, and by this humility David receives from God all that he needs; he did not rely on being a king or a military commander, nor did he rely on any resources he had, but he relied on God alone; therefore he lived at ease.

25.12.5.en: 4- By this prayer David is freed from the feeling of loneliness or isolation, and this grace is considered the sixth gift that God grants to those who fear Him.

25.13.0.en: 17- Relieve the troubles of my heart; bring thou me out of my distresses.

25.13.1.en: 1- David is exposed to feelings of distress that assail his heart as a result of many events that pass over him and close in on him, almost choking him; therefore he asks God to relieve him, and remove from him these feelings of distress, and give his heart rest.

25.13.2.en: 2- He also asks God to bring him out of the problems he meets in his life, and all the distresses that pass over him through his dealings with others, since he trusts in God's power, which is able to bring him out in peace from all troubles.

25.13.3.en: 3- David is an example of the spiritual person who fears God; he does not live an easy life but one full of problems, and the devil fights him more than others because he walks uprightly, but he is distinguished from others by God's care for him and his inner peace, because God is with him.

25.14.0.en: 18- Look upon my lowliness and my weariness; and forgive all my sins.

25.14.1.en: 1- The seventh gift that God gives to those who fear Him is the forgiveness of their sins, which is the greatest grace, because by it a person's life is renewed so that he becomes pure after being rid of his sins, however hard they were. And by this a person triumphs over his first enemy, which is sin, that is, the inner enemy.

25.14.2.en: 2- The condition for obtaining forgiveness from God is lowliness, that is, humility, and the sense of weariness, that is, the feeling of need for God; whoever feels his need and humbles himself holds fast to God and is persistent with Him, so God has mercy on him and forgives his sins.

25.15.0.en: 19- Consider mine enemies; for they are many; and they hate me with unjust hatred.

25.15.1.en: 1- David also takes refuge in God to rescue him from his outward enemies, who are the demons, and everyone who submits to Satan and walks in the way of evil and wrongs God's children, and this is the eighth gift. But God's power is greater than any power in the world; therefore when David takes refuge in God he is assured that God will save him from all his enemies.

25.15.2.en: 2- The difficulty of the situation is in the multitude of enemies, but their multitude is worthless, because God's power surpasses all their power. But the multitude of enemies made David hasten to God and ask for His help.

25.15.3.en: 3- The strange thing is that the enemies hated David although he was innocent. He was wronged, but he did not doubt and did not leave his upright way. And on the other hand his heart was not troubled so as to try to take revenge on his enemies, but he trusted in God, surrendered his life to Him, and kept his peace.

25.16.0.en: 20- O keep my soul, and deliver me: let me not be ashamed; for I put my trust in thee.

25.16.1.en: 1- David asks God to keep him in all his ways, whether he sees the enemies or does not see them. For God knows everything, and is able to keep His children from every evil and from all the devil's hidden tricks, so that God's children walk at ease in their present life and do not fear the future.

25.16.2.en: 2- When David discovered the plots of the wicked he also asked God to rescue him from them, and this confirms his faith in God's power, love and care for him. And his confidence appears in that he is assured he will not be put to shame, that is, the enemies will not prevail against him, because he trusts in God.

25.17.0.en: 21- Let integrity and uprightness preserve me; for I wait on thee.

25.17.1.en: 1- The ninth gift that God gives to those who fear Him is perfection, so He adorns them with every virtue, and they strive in the way of perfection, imitating their perfect God.

25.17.2.en: 2- David is confident that however much he is exposed to problems, or even in his weakness falls into sin, he still waits for God and hopes in Him, confident of His care for him.

25.18.0.en: 22- Redeem Israel, O God, out of all his troubles.

25.18.1.en: 1- David's love for all his people Israel appears when he asks God to redeem them and rescue them from every tribulation; he feels his membership in the community, that is, his oneness with all his brethren, and feels their feelings. The verse also shows David's fatherhood, for he asks on behalf of all his people, for whom he feels responsible.

25.18.2.en: 2- David sees that his salvation is accomplished together with the salvation of the rest of his brethren from the people of God, and he is not isolated from the rest of the believers, and God's complete salvation includes him and the rest of his brethren.

25.18.3.en: 3- By the spirit of prophecy David sees the redemption of Christ that will be accomplished in the fullness of time, when Christ redeems the new Israel, that is, all who believe in Him.

25.18.4.en: If only you would feel for all your brethren in the Church and pray for them, for God rejoices in your love and gives you and them abundant blessings.

25.18.5.en: The life of uprightness. Of David. "Judge me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity" (v. 1). Introduction:

25.18.8.en: a - When David was fleeing from the face of Saul, and Saul was accusing him at that time of betraying his people, rejecting the house of the Lord, and taking refuge in dwelling among the wicked, that is, the pagans, although he was compelled to flee because Saul wanted to kill him. And he wrote this Psalm to defend himself.

25.18.9.en: b - When Ishbosheth the son of Saul was killed by two of his servants (2 Sam 4:5-12) and the Jews accused David of killing him, he wrote this Psalm in defense of his uprightness and to prove his innocence.

25.18.10.en: c - When David fled from the face of Absalom he wrote this Psalm, because of his sense of being wronged, and he wanted to prove his uprightness.

25.18.12.en: The priests used to recite it when washing in the house of the Lord, before offering the sacrifices, to remember the purifying of their hearts before serving the Lord, and to declare before those entering the house of the Lord the conditions for entering this place, that is, purity and uprightness.

25.18.13.en: 4- This Psalm is one of the messianic Psalms, because it speaks about Christ, who is without sin, and yet was accused unjustly and bore it for us.

25.18.14.en: 5- This Psalm shares with the seventh Psalm and the seventeenth Psalm that in all these Psalms David defends his innocence.

25.18.15.en: 6- This Psalm speaks about the persecuted Church, or about any person who walks uprightly with God and is exposed to injustice and false accusations.

25.18.16.en: 7- This Psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of the Third Hour, in which false accusations were brought against Christ.
